  text: '# Conventions for new-physics coefficients\n' +
    '\n' +
    'This file is normative. Every model card, every coefficient plugin, and every derivation in `notes.md` follows it. When a paper you are translating uses a different convention, convert to this one and say so in `notes.md`.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '## 1. Units and constants\n' +
    '\n' +
    'Natural units with energies in MeV. The framework provides these constants; do not redefine them.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '| symbol | value | meaning |\n' +
    '|---|---|---|\n' +
    '| `GF` | 1.16638e-11 MeV⁻² | Fermi constant |\n' +
    '| `SQRT2` | √2 at double precision | √2 |\n' +
    '| `E_CHARGE` | 0.303 | electromagnetic coupling e (α = e²/4π) |\n' +
    '| `SIN2_THETA_W` | 0.2312 | sin²θ_W |\n' +
    '| `M_U`, `M_D` | 2.2, 4.7 MeV | current quark masses used in scalar nucleon charges |\n' +
    '| `M_P`, `M_N` | 938.27, 939.56 MeV | nucleon masses |\n' +
    '| `M_MU`, `M_TAU` | 105.658369, 1776.99 MeV | charged lepton masses |\n' +
    '\n' +
    'The values in this table are the ones exported by `nuagent.physics.couplings`, at full precision; use the exported names in plugins rather than retyping numbers. The module also exports `Q_EM` (the quark electric charges `{"u": 2/3, "d": -1/3}`) and `KAPPA_LMU_LTAU` (κ of section 6).\n' +
    '\n' +
    'Momentum transfer: the framework passes you `q2`, a numpy array of the squared spacelike momentum transfer Q² = 2 M T ≥ 0 in MeV², where M is the nuclear mass and T the nuclear recoil energy. A propagator is always `1 / (q2 + mass**2)`.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '## 2. The operator basis\n' +
    '\n' +
    'The framework describes neutrino scattering on quark f ∈ {u, d} between flavors α, β ∈ {e, μ, τ} with the effective Lagrangian\n' +
    '\n' +
    '    L_eff ⊃ −√2 G_F Σ_{α,β,f} C^{fV}_{αβ}(Q²) [ν̄_α γ^μ P_L ν_β] [f̄ γ_μ f]          (vector)\n' +
    '\n' +
    'and, for scalar exchange, with the coefficient defined in section 4. The coefficients C are dimensionless, complex, and Hermitian in the flavor indices: C_{βα} = (C_{αβ})*.\n' +
    '\n' +
    'The vector coefficient is the usual NSI combination C^{fV} = ε^{fL} + ε^{fR}. In this normalization the Standard Model values are the tree-level Z couplings\n' +
    '\n' +
    '    C^{uV}_SM = +1/2 − (4/3) sin²θ_W ≈ +0.1917,     C^{dV}_SM = −1/2 + (2/3) sin²θ_W ≈ −0.3459,\n' +
    '\n' +
    'flavor-diagonal. The framework adds radiative corrections to these itself. You never write SM values; you write only the new-physics contribution, and the framework forms the total C = C_SM + C_NP once.\n' +
    '\n' +
    'The nuclear vector charge, for the entry C_{αβ} (the operator ν̄_α … ν_β turns an incoming ν_β into an outgoing ν_α; rates are unchanged by this labeling because |C_{αβ}| = |C_{βα}|), is\n' +
    '\n' +
    '    Q^{αβ} = Z (2 C^{uV}_{αβ} + C^{dV}_{αβ}) + N (C^{uV}_{αβ} + 2 C^{dV}_{αβ}),\n' +
    '\n' +
    'and the rate is proportional to Σ_β |Q^{αβ}|². In the SM, Q^{αα} ≈ 0.04 Z − 0.5 N, which is negative. A new-physics contribution with the same sign as the SM charge interferes constructively; one with the opposite sign interferes destructively and can produce a cancellation at some coupling.\n' +
    '\n' +
    'Structures accepted in this prototype: `V` (vector) and `S` (scalar). Axial, pseudoscalar and tensor are rejected by the schema; if a description needs them, say so in `notes.md` and stop.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '## 3. Vector mediator matching\n' +
    '\n' +
    'For a new vector boson Z′ with the interaction\n' +
    '\n' +
    '    L ⊃ Z′_μ ( g_ν^{αβ} ν̄_α γ^μ P_L ν_β + g_f f̄ γ^μ f ),       mass m > 0,\n' +
    '\n' +
    'tree-level exchange gives\n' +
    '\n' +
    '    C^{fV}_{αβ}(Q²) = g_ν^{αβ} g_f / ( √2 G_F (Q² + m²) ).\n' +
    '\n' +
    'Derivation: integrating out Z′ produces −(g_ν g_f)/(Q² + m²) [ν̄γ^μP_Lν][f̄γ_μf] for spacelike exchange; compare with −√2 G_F C [ν̄γ^μP_Lν][f̄γ_μf].\n' +
    '\n' +
    'Anchor you can check in one line: insert the SM Z itself, g_ν = g/(2 cos θ_W), g_f = g g_V^f/(2 cos θ_W), m = M_Z, and use G_F/√2 = g²/(8 M_W²). Here g_V^f = T₃ − 2 Q sin²θ_W, the normalization in which the Z couples as −(g/2cos θ_W) Z_μ f̄ γ^μ (g_V − g_A γ5) f. The result is C^{fV} = g_V^f, the SM value above. A formula that returns g_V^f / 2 is missing a factor of 2.\n' +
    '\n' +
    'Known pitfall: the legacy `pyCEvNS` package mapped ε = g/(2√2 G_F m²), half of the expression above if its `g` meant g_ν g_f. Do not copy it.\n' +
    '\n' +
    'Notes on the neutrino coupling:\n' +
    '- Only the left-handed neutrino current appears. If a model writes g_ν ν̄ γ^μ ν for a Dirac neutrino with both chiralities, the right-handed part does not scatter on the SM-produced left-handed neutrinos; use the left-handed coupling.\n' +
    '- If a model writes the coupling as (g′/2) ν̄ γ^μ (1 − γ5) ν, that is g′ ν̄ γ^μ P_L ν, so g_ν = g′. If it writes g ν̄ γ^μ (1 − γ5) ν without the 1/2, then g_ν = 2g.\n' +
    '- Off-diagonal g_ν^{αβ} with α ≠ β is allowed and must be Hermitian. It enters incoherently (no interference with the SM) because the SM has no flavor-changing neutral current.\n' +
    '- Antineutrinos: the framework handles them; you supply the same C.\n' +
    '\n' +
    'Quark couplings: give g_u and g_d separately. If a model gives chiral quark couplings Z′_μ (g_L q̄_L γ^μ q_L + g_R q̄_R γ^μ q_R), the vector coupling is g_q = (g_L + g_R)/2. Note the 1/2 here against C = ε^L + ε^R with no 1/2: these are different objects, and confusing them is a second factor-2 trap. The axial part (g_R − g_L)/2 contributes nothing to coherent scattering on the spin-0 formula used in this prototype; keep the vector part and record the dropped axial coupling in `notes.md`.\n' +
    '\n' +
    "Nucleon-level inputs: nucleon couplings are not card fields, but they convert exactly to quark couplings, because the framework's nuclear charge is Q = Z g_p + N g_n with g_p = 2 g_u + g_d and g_n = g_u + 2 g_d. Given g_p and g_n:\n" +
    '\n' +
    '    g_u = (2 g_p − g_n) / 3,     g_d = (2 g_n − g_p) / 3.\n' +
    '\n' +
    'A protophobic Z′ (g_p = 0) therefore has g_u = −g_n/3 and g_d = 2 g_n/3; a coupling to baryon number (g_p = g_n = g_B) has g_u = g_d = g_B/3.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '## 4. Scalar mediator matching\n' +
    '\n' +
    'For a scalar φ with\n' +
    '\n' +
    '    L ⊃ φ ( g_ν^{αβ} ν̄_α ν_β + Σ_q g_q q̄ q ),       mass m > 0,\n' +
    '\n' +
    'the scalar coefficient is defined, dimensionless like the vector one, as\n' +
    '\n' +
    '    C^{qS}_{αβ}(Q²) = g_ν^{αβ} g_q / ( √2 G_F (Q² + m²) ),\n' +
    '\n' +
    'and the framework forms the nuclear scalar charge\n' +
    '\n' +
    '    Q_S^{αβ}(Q²) = √2 G_F Σ_q C^{qS}_{αβ}(Q²) ( Z m_p f_q^p + N m_n f_q^n ) / m_q,\n' +
    '\n' +
    'with f_u^p = 0.0208, f_d^p = 0.0411, f_u^n = 0.0189, f_d^n = 0.0451. For a single mediator this is g_ν (Z c_p + N c_n)/(Q² + m²) with c_N = m_N Σ_q g_q f_q^N / m_q. Numerically, for g_u = g_d = g_q, c_p ≈ c_n ≈ 17.1 g_q, so the nucleus couples as roughly 17 A g_q.\n' +
    '\n' +
    'The scalar amplitude flips the neutrino helicity and does not interfere with the SM or with vector new physics. Its rate is proportional to Σ_β |Q_S^{αβ}|² with a different kinematic factor, which the framework supplies. You do not write cross sections.\n' +
    '\n' +
    'Notes:\n' +
    '- ν̄_α ν_β requires a right-handed neutrino (Dirac) or a Majorana mass-type coupling. State which in `notes.md`; the coefficient is the same at this level.\n' +
    "- If a model gives nucleon-level scalar couplings y_p and y_n, convert to quark couplings by solving the two linear equations c_p = y_p and c_n = y_n, that is m_p (g_u f_u^p/m_u + g_d f_d^p/m_d) = y_p and m_n (g_u f_u^n/m_u + g_d f_d^n/m_d) = y_n. For y_p = y_n = y the solution is g_u = 0.058970 y and g_d = 0.058122 y. This reproduces the framework's nuclear scalar charge exactly.\n" +
    '- Only u and d scalar couplings can be represented. A model whose scalar couples to heavier quarks with non-negligible weight (for example a Higgs-portal scalar with g_q ∝ m_q, where heavy quarks dominate the nucleon coupling through the gluon term) cannot be expressed here: say so in `notes.md` and stop.\n' +
    '- For a Majorana neutrino the statement that the coefficient is unchanged holds when the mass-type term is written (g_ν/2) φ ν̄ ν; written without the 1/2, the vertex doubles and g_ν must be doubled accordingly.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '## 5. Contact interactions\n' +
    '\n' +
    'A card may list `contacts`: constant ε^{fV}_{αβ} that are added directly to C^{fV}. Use them only when the description gives epsilons rather than a mediator. If a mass is given, use the mediator form in both the plugin and the card, however heavy the mediator: the contact form differs by Q²/m², which reaches about 1 percent at m = 1 GeV at the top of the COHERENT recoil range and fails the 1e-6 cross-check for any mass below about 100 GeV. Contact scalar entries are not supported.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '## 6. Kinetic mixing\n' +
    '\n' +
    'For a vector mediator, the card field `kinetic_mixing` ε adds an electromagnetic-charge-proportional coupling to every charged fermion:\n' +
    '\n' +
    '    g_q → g_q + ε e Q_q^em,       Q_u^em = +2/3,   Q_d^em = −1/3,   e = 0.303.\n' +
    '\n' +
    "This is the low-energy coupling of a Z′ that mixes with the photon. The sign of ε relative to the other couplings is part of the model and must be stated in `notes.md`. Mapping from Lagrangian conventions: with a kinetic term −(ε_L/2) F_μν Z′^μν and covariant derivative D_μ = ∂_μ + i e Q A_μ, the Z′ acquires +ε_L e Q f̄ γ^μ f, so ε = ε_L; with D_μ = ∂_μ − i e Q A_μ the sign flips. Mixing with hypercharge ε_Y gives ε = ε_Y cos θ_W for m ≪ M_Z. Models with Z–Z′ mass mixing, such as the dark-hypercharge and dark-Z cases of arXiv:1803.01224 (its equations 7 and 8), give Z′ couplings proportional to hypercharge or to the Z current, neutrinos included; take g_ν and g_q from the paper's coupling formula rather than from `kinetic_mixing` alone.\n" +
    '\n' +
    'Loop-induced mixing for U(1)_{L_μ−L_τ}: muon and tau loops generate, at Q² ≪ m_μ²,\n' +
    '\n' +
    '    ε = + κ g′,     κ = e ln(m_τ/m_μ) / (6 π²) = 0.0144417637.\n' +
    '\n' +
    "The sign is a physics result, not a convention. The induced quark coupling is g_q = e Q_q Σ_ℓ (g′ Q′_ℓ)(e Q_ℓ) ln(m_ℓ²)/(12π²): the m-independent part of the loop cancels because Σ_ℓ Q′_ℓ Q_ℓ = 0, and the ln(m²) term carries the sign that makes the running electromagnetic coupling grow with Q². With Q′_μ = +1, Q′_τ = −1 and Q_ℓ = −1 the sum is +ln(m_τ²/m_μ²) > 0, so ε = +κ g′. Intuition: the proton's screening cloud holds more μ⁻ than τ⁻ because the muon is lighter, and μ⁻ carries L_μ−L_τ charge +1 like ν_μ, so the induced proton coupling has the same sign as the ν_μ coupling and the interference with the SM is destructive for ν_μ. The template `zprime_lmu_ltau` fills ε = κ g′ when no `kinetic_mixing` is given; a card has no such default, so write the value explicitly (κ times g′, at full precision).   name: 'plugin_api.md',
  text: '# Coefficient plugin API\n' +
    '\n' +
    'A coefficient plugin is one Python module. The framework imports it by path, reads three names, and calls one function.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '```python\n' +
    'import numpy as np\n' +
    'from nuagent.physics.couplings import Coefficients, GF, SQRT2, E_CHARGE\n' +
    '\n' +
    'PARAMETERS = {"g_nu": 1e-4, "g_q": 1e-4, "mass_mev": 30.0}   # defaults; every key is a parameter\n' +
    'COUPLINGS = ("g_nu", "g_q")                                   # the subset that are couplings\n' +
    '\n' +
    'def coefficients(q2: np.ndarray, params: dict[str, float]) -> Coefficients:\n' +
    '    c = Coefficients.zeros(q2)                                 # all structures, quarks, flavors at zero\n' +
    '    value = params["g_nu"] * params["g_q"] / (SQRT2 * GF * (q2 + params["mass_mev"] ** 2))\n' +
    '    for quark in ("u", "d"):\n' +
    '        for pair in ("ee", "mm", "tt"):\n' +
    '            c.set("V", quark, pair, value)                     # value: scalar or array shaped like q2\n' +
    '    return c\n' +
    '```\n' +
    '\n' +
    'Contract:\n' +
    '\n' +
    '- `coefficients` returns the new-physics contribution only. Never add Standard Model values.\n' +
    '- `q2` is a 1D array of Q² = 2 M T in MeV², all entries ≥ 0. Return values broadcast over it.\n' +
    '- `Coefficients.set(structure, quark, pair, value)` with `structure` in `{"V", "S"}`, `quark` in `{"u", "d"}`, `pair` in `{"ee","mm","tt","em","et","mt"}`. Setting `em` also sets `me` to the complex conjugate. Diagonal values must be real; a complex diagonal value raises `ValueError`.\n' +
    '- `c.values[structure, quark]` is the complex array shaped `(3, 3, len(q2))` behind `set`, indexed by (α, β) in the order e, μ, τ. Read it to inspect values; write through `set`.\n' +
    '- `COUPLINGS` lists the parameter names that are couplings. The framework sets all of them to zero to check that your plugin reproduces the Standard Model, and checks each is at most √(4π) in magnitude.\n' +
    '- `PARAMETERS` defaults are the parameter point of the description. The harness evaluates the proposed point there, and the eval scores coefficients there.\n' +
    '- Parameters are real numbers. A complex off-diagonal entry is built inside `coefficients` from separate real and imaginary parameters.\n' +
    '- `set` overwrites. Sum every contribution to an entry (for example two mediators) before calling `set` once.\n' +
    '- Pure functions only: no file or network access, no randomness, no global state. Use `numpy` and the constants exported by `nuagent.physics.couplings`.\n' +
    '- Keep the derivation in `notes.md`, not in comments.\n' +
    '\n' +
    "A raw cross-section plugin (escape hatch) instead exposes `dsigma_dt(e_nu, t, flavor, isotope, params) -> np.ndarray` returning the complete differential cross section including the Standard Model in MeV⁻³, plus the same `PARAMETERS` and `COUPLINGS`. `t` is a scalar or a 1D array of recoil energies in MeV and `e_nu` broadcasts against it; the result has the broadcast shape. `flavor` is one of `e, mu, tau, ebar, mubar, taubar`; `isotope` is a `nuagent.physics.xsec.Isotope` with attributes `z`, `n`, `mass_mev` and `helm_radius_fm` (the experiment's Helm radius), and `isotope.q2(t)` gives Q² = 2 M T. It is written by users, not by the agent: it must include the framework's SM cross section with the experiment's form factor, which it obtains as `nuagent.physics.xsec.dsigma_dt(e_nu, t, flavor, isotope, nuagent.physics.couplings.sm(isotope.q2(t)))`. It is used only for physics outside the basis (magnetic moments, inelastic channels), it skips the SM-limit check, and its report is labeled `raw-cross-section`. If a description needs physics outside the V and S basis, write `notes.md` naming the raw route and produce no plugin.\n" +
    '\n' +
    'When a description within the V and S basis leaves the mass, a coupling or the Lorentz structure open, write `questions.json` and `notes.md` instead of a plugin or card:\n' +
    '\n' +
    '```json\n' +
    '{"questions": [\n' +
    '  {"id": "mass_mev", "question": "What is the mediator mass?", "unit": "MeV", "suggested": 10,\n' +
    '   "reason": "10 MeV is a common light-mediator benchmark; the description gives no mass."},\n' +
    '  {"id": "g_d", "question": "What is the vector coupling to down quarks?", "unit": null, "suggested": null, "reason": null}\n' +
    ']}\n' +
    '```\n' +
    '\n' +
    '- `questions` is a nonempty list. Each entry has exactly the fields `id`, `question`, `unit`, `suggested` and `reason`.\n' +
    "- `id` is a short `snake_case` identifier, unique in the file and never `free_text` (reserved for the user's free-text answer). When the question asks for a quantity that becomes a plugin parameter, `id` is that parameter's name.\n" +
    '- `question` is one sentence. `unit` is a string or null.\n' +
    '- `suggested` is a number (not a boolean), a string or null. Suggest only a conventional benchmark, never a value presented as part of the description.\n' +
    '- `reason` is one sentence saying where the suggestion comes from, or null when `suggested` is null.\n' +
    '- `questions.json` beside `plugin.py` or `card.json`, or a file that does not match this shape, is a validation finding. Example 07 shows a complete questions outcome.\n' +
    '\n' +
    '`example_plugin.py` is a standalone runnable coefficient plugin. For example, from the repository root:\n' +
    '\n' +
    '```bash\n' +
    'uv run nuagent predict --experiment coherent_csi_2017 --plugin src/nuagent/context/example_plugin.py\n' +
    '```\n' +
    '\n' +
    'Validation inside a task directory uses:\n' +
    '\n' +
    '```bash\n' +
    'nuagent validate --plugin plugin.py --card card.json\n' +
    '```\n' +
    '\n' +
    'With both files present the command will also cross-check that the plugin and the card agree on every coefficient at a grid of Q² values. See `framework.md` for what this evidence can establish and what it cannot.\n'
}{

## 7. U(1)′ charge assignments

For a gauged U(1)′ with gauge coupling g′ and charges Q′: g_ν^{αα} = g′ Q′_{ν_α}, g_q = g′ Q′_q, flavor-diagonal unless the charges are flavor off-diagonal in the mass basis (rare; then give the matrix). Common assignments:

| model | Q′_{ν_e} | Q′_{ν_μ} | Q′_{ν_τ} | Q′_u | Q′_d | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B − L | −1 | −1 | −1 | +1/3 | +1/3 | g_ν g_q < 0: constructive with the SM |
| universal (toy) | +1 | +1 | +1 | +1 | +1 | g_ν g_q > 0: destructive, cancellation possible |
| L_μ − L_τ | 0 | +1 | −1 | 0 | 0 | quarks only via kinetic mixing |
| B − 3L_τ | 0 | 0 | −3 | +1/3 | +1/3 | |
| B − 3L_e | −3 | 0 | 0 | +1/3 | +1/3 | |

The neutrino charge is the charge of the lepton doublet. Anomaly cancellation is the model author's concern, not the framework's; mention in `notes.md` if a requested assignment is anomalous.

## 8. Flavor matrices

A flavor matrix is given by six entries `ee, mm, tt, em, et, mt`. Diagonal entries are real. Off-diagonal entries may be complex, written as `[re, im]`; the framework fills the conjugate partner. `em` means the (e, μ) entry, that is C_{eμ}.

## 9. What the framework does for you

Given your coefficients, the framework: adds the SM; forms the nuclear charges for each isotope of the detector; evaluates the differential cross section with the Helm form factor; folds it with the experiment's neutrino flux for each flavor; applies efficiency, quenching, exposure and binning; and compares with observed counts. You never need the flux, the detector, the form factor, or the SM couplings.

## 10. Perturbativity and sanity

Every dimensionless coupling you write must satisfy |g| ≤ √(4π) ≈ 3.54. Masses are in MeV and positive. If a description gives a coupling in a different normalization (for example α′ = g′²/4π), convert and show the conversion.

Write `questions.json` with one question per missing input (shape in `plugin_api.md`) and `notes.md` saying exactly what is missing, and produce no plugin or card. # Example 01: flavor-universal vector mediator

Description given to the agent: "A new vector boson Z′ of mass 30 MeV that couples with the same strength g′ = 1e-4 to all three left-handed neutrino flavors and to up and down quarks."

## Derivation

1. Lorentz structure: vector exchange, so structure `V`.
2. Couplings as written: g_ν^{ee} = g_ν^{mm} = g_ν^{tt} = g′, off-diagonal zero; g_u = g_d = g′.
3. Matching (conventions section 3): C^{uV}_{αα} = C^{dV}_{αα} = g′² / (√2 G_F (Q² + m²)).
4. Sign: g_ν g_q = +g′² > 0, so the nuclear charge shift ΔQ = (3Z + 3N) C is positive while Q_SM is negative: destructive interference. At the first reference point ΔQ = 113.1, larger than |Q_SM| = 36.9, so the total charge has changed sign and the rate is about (76.2/36.9)² ≈ 4.3 times the SM there. Two couplings are worth knowing at this Q² (tree level; with radiative corrections in parentheses): exact cancellation of the charge, hence almost no coherent rate, near g′ ≈ 5.71e-05 (5.82e-05), which is excluded; and ΔQ = −2 Q_SM near g′ ≈ 8.08e-05 (8.23e-05), where the rate equals the SM again. The second is the origin of the degenerate band in universal-Z′ limits.
5. Card-expressible: yes, one mediator entry.

Reference points: Q² = 2 M T for Cs-133 (M = 123.8 GeV) at T = 5, 15, 25 keV, i.e. Q² = 1238, 3714, 6190 MeV². SM tree-level nuclear charge for Cs-133: Q_SM = -36.93 (negative; with the framework's radiative corrections it is -38.28). Tabulated values are rounded to five digits for reading; eval expectations are generated at full precision from the exported constants.

## Expected coefficients

| coefficient | Q²=1238 | Q²=3714 | Q²=6190 |
|---|---|---|---|
| C^{uV}_ee = C^{uV}_mm = C^{uV}_tt | 2.8355e-01 | 1.3139e-01 | 8.5506e-02 |
| C^{dV}_ee = C^{dV}_mm = C^{dV}_tt | 2.8355e-01 | 1.3139e-01 | 8.5506e-02 |

All off-diagonal entries and all scalar entries are zero.

import numpy as np
from nuagent.physics.couplings import Coefficients, GF, SQRT2

PARAMETERS = {"g_prime": 1e-4, "mass_mev": 30.0}
COUPLINGS = ("g_prime",)

def coefficients(q2: np.ndarray, params: dict) -> Coefficients:
    c = Coefficients.zeros(q2)
    value = params["g_prime"] ** 2 / (SQRT2 * GF * (q2 + params["mass_mev"] ** 2))
    for quark in ("u", "d"):
        for pair in ("ee", "mm", "tt"):
            c.set("V", quark, pair, value)
